subject: [Escalation] Clarity: intermittent streaming output freeze impacting promo event
messages:
From: Oliver Park <oliver@clarity.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-15T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected quiet windows in streaming during promo spike

Nikhil —

We started seeing a problem around 09:55 PDT during a promotional spike. Several user sessions show the token stream arriving normally for ~10–20 tokens, then the socket goes quiet for 12–30 seconds and finally resumes mid-output (or times out). In some cases the client drops the connection and the full response never delivers. Our mobile app reports this as a hard failure for chat replies.

Impact: ~8% of requests to /v1/streams returned partial responses or timed out between 09:55–10:10. Overall throughput dropped ~40% because clients are retrying and hitting backoff. This is causing visible user errors during the promo. Can you confirm if anything in your infra would cause chunk buffering or backpressure leading to delayed frames?

I attached a small sample of prod logs and request traces. Happy to hop on a call — we’re on a tight timeline for the campaign.

— Oliver
Clarity Platform Reliability

Attachments: prod-logs-20280815.txt, request-traces-10-11am-aug15.json
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Park <oliver@clarity.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-15T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected quiet windows in streaming during promo spike

Oliver — thank you for the quick report and the logs.

First pass: I’m looking at the traces you attached. I see elevated server-side queueing (avg token emission gap increased) and a cluster-level retry cascade from 09:54–10:03. Not obvious at a glance whether this is service-worker backpressure, proxy buffering, or client-side socket handling.

Immediate steps we’re taking:
- I’ve kicked off a priority job to pull relevant node logs and sproc metrics for the time window.
- Looping in Grace (CS lead) and Ben (on-call infra) to get telemetry and reproduce.
- Can you confirm the SDK version your clients are using and whether you have a mobile proxy that could be coalescing frames?

I’ll follow up shortly with an initial mitigation plan. For now, please keep that trace sample coming if you see new examples.

— Nikhil
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected quiet windows in streaming during promo spike

Adding infra detail from initial triage:

Observations (09:50–10:05 window):
- P50 token gap climbed from ~35ms to ~420ms for the Clarity tenant behind the proxy.
- Error rate (5xx + client disconnects) rose from baseline 0.7% to ~12% for affected routes.
- One routing node showed GC spikes and thread contention coincident with backpressure. Heap graphs attached to internal ticket.

Probable contributors:
1) Routing node transient CPU/GC causing delayed kernel writes for chunked responses.
2) Proxy layer coalescing small writes when under load (we saw increased TCP push coalescence).
3) Client-side socket watchdogs that treat a ~15s silence as fatal and drop.

Short-term mitigations we can push in next 30–60 minutes:
- Bypass the proxy path for Clarity to a less-used routing pool (hotfix config).
- Increase chunk flush frequency on the serving runtime for this tenant (decrease write coalescing).
- Notify Clarity to bump client socket timeout to 45s as a temporary tolerance.

Ben (on-call)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-15T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected quiet windows in streaming during promo spike

Looping in Tessa (SRE lead) and Markus (runtime) for immediate action and exec summary.

Customer impact is high (promo active). We need an exec sync at 16:15 PDT to brief C-suite and Clarity’s leadership on remediation timeline and credit request.

Triage plan for 12:30–14:00:
- Runtime patch to lower kernel write coalescing and force smaller, more frequent chunks for Clarity (Markus).
- Routing hotfix to shift traffic to a dedicated pool for the next 2 hours (Ben + infra).
- CS playbook: notify product and mobile teams at Clarity to increase socket timeout and disable client-side aggressive retry for 1 hour (Nikhil to coordinate).

We should prepare a short executive one-pager with root-cause hypothesis, immediate mitigations, and next-steps for the 16:15 sync. Nikhil — can you draft the customer-facing note and include impact metrics?

— Grace
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-15T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected quiet windows in streaming during promo spike

I deployed the runtime throttle/flush change to the Clarity routing tag at 13:00 PDT and started routing a subset (~15%) of traffic to the reserved pool at 13:12 PDT. Early signals: token gap p50 improved to ~110ms on the reserved pool and client disconnects dropped ~60% for the routed subset.

However, the old pool still shows periodic 10–20s quiet windows. Ben — we need the full shift to reserved routing to complete and a probe to validate no regression in throughput.

I’ll prepare the exec slide with graphs (before/after) and attach the probe dashboard.

— Markus
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Park <oliver@clarity.ai>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-15T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: [ACTION & Exec Sync] Clarity streaming quiet-window escalation — brief and next steps

Oliver, quick status before the 16:15 exec sync: thank you again for surfacing the traces. Here’s a concise summary for your leadership and ours.

Impact summary (9:54–13:30 PDT window):
- Symptom: intermittent ~12–25s output silence on chunked/WebSocket streaming requests. Clients often treat this as a hard failure.
- Customer-visible: ~8–12% affected sessions during the peak; effective throughput for Clarity routes dropped ~40% due to retries/backoff.
- Error rate: rose to ~12% (5xx + disconnects) at peak.

Actions taken (completed / in-progress):
- 13:00 PDT: runtime flush frequency adjusted for Clarity (smaller chunks).
- 13:12 PDT: partial traffic reroute to reserved pool; routed subset shows p50 token gap down to ~110ms and disconnects -60%.
- Infra is finishing the full traffic migration; we expect majority traffic on reserved pool within 30 minutes.
- CS recommendation: temporarily increase client socket timeout to 45s; avoid aggressive client-side retry.

Next steps and asks:
1) Short-term (next hour): complete full routing shift, monitor for residual quiet windows.
2) Mid-term (48–72h): deeper RCA on root cause (suspected proxy coalescing + routing node GC interactions) and a code fix to reduce coalescing under load.
3) Compensation: Clarity team — we’re prepared to discuss usage credits for the impacted window. Nikhil will own the customer communication and credit proposal.

Exec sync: 16:15 PDT (15 min) — join link in thread. We’ll share the one-pager and live dashboards.

Oliver — can you confirm attendance from your side? Also confirm whether your mobile team can accept the 45s temporary timeout today.

— Nikhil
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
